voice: Calm and blunt. Second person. Never shouts, never hypes, never says hustle or grindset. The whole point of the name is that it is quiet: the delivery is a flat, certain voice telling you something uncomfortable and true. No rhetorical questions. No lists. No calls to subscribe inside the script.
formula: HOOK: one specific uncomfortable observation, not a platitude. MECHANISM: two or three sentences on why it is actually true, concrete, ideally naming a number or a process. STAKES: one sentence on what it costs you. ACTION: one small thing, doable today, no equipment.
audience: 14 to 19 year olds who already suspect they are wasting time and want the reason, not the pep talk.
rules: No em dashes anywhere, the voice engine reads them as pauses in the wrong place.
No quotes from famous people. Original scripts only. Quote-card channels are what YouTube's inauthentic content policy targets and they do not build an audience that trusts you.
Never promise money or results. Say what the mechanism is and let the viewer draw it.
80 words is the target. At the Andrew voice +12% that lands around 30 seconds.

bank.hook: A bad session still counts
bank.script: There is a version of today where you do forty per cent of what you planned, and you should take it. Half a session keeps you a person who trains. Zero sessions, even once, starts quietly rewriting that, and the rewrite is far more expensive than the lost work. You are not protecting your standards by skipping when you cannot do it properly. You are protecting your mood. Lower today's bar until it is almost embarrassing, then clear it. You can be strict again tomorrow, from a streak you did not break.

bank.hook: Out of sight beats self control
bank.script: The phone face down on the desk is still winning. You are not reading, you are waiting, and part of your attention is permanently parked on whether it lit up. Being in the room is the whole problem, because resisting something nearby costs you continuously, and you are spending that on top of the actual work. Distance is cheaper than discipline, every single time. Put it in another room, not your pocket, not face down, not on silent. Another room, for one session. Notice how much easier the work gets.

bank.emphasis: face down, still winning, you are waiting, permanently parked, in the room, costs you continuously, on top of the work, distance is cheaper, another room

bank.hook: Anchor it to a time, not a feeling
bank.script: If your session happens whenever you get round to it, it is competing with everything else in the day and it will lose, because everything else is louder and has deadlines. A fixed time is not about being rigid. It is about the thing having a place that is already defended, so you are not relitigating it against your mood every afternoon. Pick a time that is realistic on your worst day, not your best. Then protect it like something else put it in your calendar, because in a sense it did.

bank.hook: You cannot see it from inside
bank.script: Progress is almost impossible to notice while it is happening, because you improve and your standards improve at the same rate, so the gap between where you are and where you want to be looks identical every week. That is why eight good weeks can feel like nothing. The only honest check is a record: what you lifted, how fast you read, what you could not do in January. Write down one measurable thing today and do not look at it again until the end of the month.

bank.emphasis: impossible to notice, standards improve, same rate, looks identical, eight good weeks, feel like nothing, honest check, a record, could not do in January, end of the month

bank.hook: You are roughly the average of your last ten days
bank.script: Not your best day, which you remember, and not your worst, which you defend. The average, which you never actually look at. One brilliant session does not move an average much, and that is why a huge effort followed by five days off leaves you where you started, feeling cheated. The boring middle is what the average is made of. Stop aiming at remarkable days. Aim at raising the floor, and ask what the laziest acceptable version of your day looks like, then make that the default.

bank.hook: Announcing it spends the feeling
bank.script: Telling people your plan gives you a small hit of the thing you were supposed to earn by doing it. You get the nods, the you-will-smash-it, a bit of the identity, all before any work exists. Having been paid in advance, you are measurably less likely to follow through, which is the opposite of what accountability is supposed to do. Keep the next one quiet until there is something real to point at. Do four sessions before you tell a single person it is happening.
bank.keywords: alone silent night training no audience dark solitary

bank.hook: Rest is part of the plan, not a prize
bank.script: You treat rest as something you have to deserve, so you either skip it and get worse, or take it badly and feel guilty the whole time, which means it does not even work. Rest is not the opposite of the work. It is the part where the work gets absorbed, and scheduling it on purpose is what lets you push properly on the days in between. Put one real rest day in your week, now, in advance. Not when you collapse. Chosen, written down and taken without apology.
